reasoning.title: Verify counts in the visible commit history
reasoning.description: Use when counting one author’s commits on a specific date within a GitLab project; do not use the Contributors view, which aggregates activity and does not provide a reliable date-level count.
reasoning.content: Open “Repository” → “Commits,” select the intended branch, then scroll or paginate until the requested date heading and its complete commit group are visibly rendered; if accessibility output omits the rows, continue scrolling, inspect the rendered page, or open commit details rather than narrating unseen data. Enumerate every commit in that date group across page boundaries whose displayed author exactly matches the requested name, treating near-identical name variants as distinct unless visible profile or email evidence proves they are the same, and report only the evidenced count.

reasoning.title: Use structured contribution filters
reasoning.description: Apply when identifying every project a user contributed to, especially if the profile’s “Contributed projects” tab is empty or incomplete; do not use this when only projects containing a literal phrase are requested.
reasoning.content: Start with the profile’s “Contributed projects” tab; if it is unavailable, use contribution-bearing views such as “Merge requests” with the “Author” filter set to the user and “Any status,” rather than global full-text search for the display name. Enumerate every result page and union the full project paths, checking other relevant contribution scopes as needed; an empty profile tab or a few text matches does not establish completeness.

reasoning.title: Verify stars on each project
reasoning.description: Apply after obtaining candidate project paths when the answer depends on a star threshold; do not infer stars from Explore sorting or unlabeled project statistics.
reasoning.content: Open each candidate’s project overview and read the value attached to the visible “Star” control, since nearby statistics may instead represent issues, forks, or merge requests. Keep only projects strictly above the requested threshold, and copy the complete namespace and repository name from the project breadcrumbs, opening the project if a result row abbreviates it.

reasoning.title: Verify the filtered commit history
reasoning.description: Use when asked to count commits by author on a specific date; do not use the project-wide commit total or Contributors report, which cannot establish a date-specific count.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Commits, select the required branch or scope, and navigate or filter until the requested date’s commit group is displayed; continue through pagination or “Load more” so the full date is covered. Count every row on that date whose displayed author exactly matches each requested person, opening commit details when names are abbreviated and keeping distinct near-identical author identities separate; then sum the verified per-author counts only.

reasoning.title: Verify the top relevant project
reasoning.description: Use when “best” means the highest-starred public project matching a subject and language; do not use when the user defines another quality measure.
reasoning.content: Open “Explore” → “Projects,” search the subject, select “Most stars,” and visibly inspect the result rows for star count, relevance, and the required language; check all result pages and every tied top row before choosing. Do not infer ranking from a project’s name or description alone, and do not treat the first opened result as confirmed unless the sorted results and qualification evidence are visible.

reasoning.title: Copy SSH command from the Clone menu
reasoning.description: Use after the winning repository has been verified and an exact SSH clone command is requested.
reasoning.content: On the project’s repository page, open the visible “Code” or “Clone” dropdown and copy the complete value labeled “Clone with SSH”; if GitLab displays only the URL, prefix that exact value with `git clone `. Never reconstruct the SSH host, port, namespace, capitalization, or suffix from the browser URL, project heading, or SSH-key warning, and do not answer until the menu’s displayed SSH value has been observed.

reasoning.title: Verify the top matching project
reasoning.description: Apply when the task asks for the most-starred repository matching a concept; do not use this when a specific repository is already named.
reasoning.content: Use global “Search GitLab,” select the “Projects” results view, and compare the visible star count for every semantically qualifying project across all result pages; if the phrase has no results, broaden terms methodically and verify relevance from each project’s description or README. Do not treat the first broad-keyword hit or the currently visible page as the complete candidate set, and report every tie at the highest count.

reasoning.title: Expose and copy the SSH clone value
reasoning.description: Apply after the correct project has been verified and an SSH clone command or URL is requested; do not infer it from the browser address, namespace, or SSH-key warning.
reasoning.content: On the project’s repository overview, open the visible “Clone” control and locate the field labeled “Clone with SSH”; keep the menu open until the complete value is visibly observed, using its copy control if available. Copy the entire displayed SSH value without truncation or substitution, and add the standard clone executable only when the interface displays a URL rather than a complete command.

reasoning.title: Use the branch commit history and a verified author identity
reasoning.description: Applies when counting one contributor’s commits within a date interval in a GitLab project; do not use the Contributors summary when an exact bounded range is required.
reasoning.content: Open “Repository” → “Commits” and select the intended branch, then use the visible “Author” control with the contributor’s GitLab username obtained from an author profile; avoid assuming that a typed name filtered anything unless a suggestion was selected and the list visibly changed. If filtering remains unavailable, inspect the dated commit groups directly rather than relying on browser Find, which may search only rendered content.

reasoning.title: Prove both date boundaries before aggregating
reasoning.description: Applies to long or lazily rendered commit histories where accessibility output truncates and repeated scrolling appears not to expose older groups; not needed when the filtered result fits on one complete page.
reasoning.content: Advance through every page or loaded segment until the first group older than the lower boundary is visible, and verify the final group inside the interval completely—seeing only its heading is insufficient. Enumerate every qualifying commit across all groups/pages, matching the full author identity rather than near-identical names, and return the count only after both boundaries and all intervening rows are accounted for.

reasoning.title: Use the branch Commit history and preserve the current host
reasoning.description: Apply when counting an author’s commits within a date range; do not use the Contributors report, which is aggregated and may not support the required date filtering.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Commits, select the requested branch, and repeatedly use the bottom loading control or scroll to the end until entries older than the target range appear; browser Find only searches rows already loaded. If using the commits API as a fallback, derive the origin and URL-encoded project path from the current page rather than inventing a hostname or namespace, and pass branch, start, end, and pagination parameters.

reasoning.title: Count the complete bounded set
reasoning.description: Apply after the commit list or API results cover the requested interval, especially when author autocomplete returns no selectable match.
reasoning.content: Do not treat an empty Author autocomplete as proof that no matching commits exist; inspect every commit row from the first through the last day of the interval and count the exact displayed author identity, checking commit details when a name is abbreviated. Continue through every loaded page or API page, include all qualifying rows, exclude boundary dates outside the interval, and keep near-identical author-name or email variants separate unless the task clearly identifies them as the same person.

reasoning.title: Recover the GitLab host, then use Repository analytics
reasoning.description: Apply when a direct project URL fails with a DNS/name-resolution error or when contributor rankings are needed; do not treat the error page as evidence that the project is missing.
reasoning.content: Return to the configured GitLab base URL or home page, verify the hostname resolves, then locate the project through the visible search control and open **Analyze → Repository analytics** (or the repository’s **Contributors** view). Avoid **Members**, activity feeds, and contributor-profile pages, which do not rank authors by repository commit count; in the analytics view, read the full contributor name and commit total, inspect every loaded/paginated row, and report every contributor tied for the highest displayed commit count without merging near-identical identities.

reasoning.title: Use Repository Contributors, not Analytics
reasoning.description: Applies when ranking a GitLab project’s contributors by commits; not when aggregate repository activity or timing charts are requested.
reasoning.content: Open the project, expand the “Repository” section in project navigation, and select the “Contributors” link; avoid “Analytics” → “Repository,” which shows aggregate charts rather than the contributor ranking. Confirm that contributor rows and commit totals have actually rendered before extracting anything.

reasoning.title: Require visible rows and honor the requested rank count
reasoning.description: Applies when contributor names and commit totals must be read from a ranked list, especially if content loads asynchronously, extends below the fold, or contains ties.
reasoning.content: Scroll, wait, and inspect every rendered contributor row and any pagination until the requested cutoff and all tied rows at that boundary are visibly verified; copy each displayed name and commit total exactly, without relying on narration or assumptions. If the request specifies a fixed number, return exactly that many unless it explicitly defines a tie-expansion rule; otherwise note a boundary tie separately rather than silently adding extra people.

reasoning.title: Verify the project Members roster before answering
reasoning.description: Use when asked who can access a GitLab project; do not use the activity feed, project list, namespace header, or a guessed profile as evidence of access.
reasoning.content: Open the target project, expand “Project information,” and select “Members”; then scroll into the page’s main content and inspect all member/access sections, including inherited or group-provided access rather than stopping when the Members page title loads. Read each row’s exact username from the profile link or open the profile if only a display name is shown, exclude the requesting user when asked who else has access, and enumerate every qualifying account across all pagination or load-more controls without guessing from near-identical names.

reasoning.title: Prove the branch leader from the complete history
reasoning.description: Use when asked for the contributor with the most commits on a particular branch; do not rely on the project-wide commit count, default branch, or the initially visible commit rows.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Commits and use the branch selector to choose the exact existing branch; if Repository → Contributors offers a branch/ref selector, select the same ref and use its aggregate, otherwise paginate or load the commit history to the end and count every author. Avoid treating the first page or a similarly named branch as conclusive, and aggregate identity variants only when commit metadata confirms they share the same author email; include every tied leader.

reasoning.title: Extract email from same-origin commit metadata
reasoning.description: Use after the leading author has been conclusively established, especially when the profile link does not navigate or the profile hides email; do not infer an address from a display name.
reasoning.content: Open one of that author’s commits, then use Options → Email Patches or navigate to the commit’s patch endpoint on the current GitLab origin with a fully qualified URL, and copy the complete address from the patch’s author/From header. Verify that the patch author matches the counted contributor and distinguish author email from committer email; do not switch to the public GitLab domain or report an unobserved value.

reasoning.title: Verify the exact ref in Contributors
reasoning.description: Use when asked for a contributor commit aggregate on a specific branch, especially when the project opens on another default branch or the ref selector does not immediately return the requested branch.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Contributors, select the exact branch result, and verify both the URL/ref and the heading “Commits to …” before reading anything; if the selector stalls, preserve the current origin and project namespace and navigate directly to the Contributors graph for the URL-encoded ref, rather than searching only Stale branches or substituting the default branch. Once the correct report loads, inspect every contributor row and every page, compare the full displayed commit counts, include all tied leaders if relevant, and report the complete maximum value without confusing similarly named refs or contributors.

reasoning.title: Recover from failed controls without changing sites
reasoning.description: Use when a visible tab or branch selector repeatedly times out, or when direct navigation is needed to confirm that the requested ref exists.
reasoning.content: Treat a timeout as an interaction failure, not proof that the branch or view is absent: use the visible All tab, reload the resulting all-branches URL, submit the branch Search, or construct the exact commits/graph path on the current page’s origin and namespace. After reaching the exact-ref Contributors report, verify its branch label and extract the aggregate from the report itself—not from the commit list, a stale-only branch view, or an aggregate for a near-identical/default ref—and review all result pages before choosing the highest count.
